gate_scope: LIMITED supported event checker only: stable-window sampling, Standard/Dual/Quad data segments (no Dual/Quad bidirectional), hardware reset. Dummy segments and software-reset completion are still unresolved; they do not pass. This is not a certification of spi_host_core. B/C is not authorized. Finite controls are not formal proof.

findings.detail: With all CSB lines high, an SCK change is accepted only if it moves to the CPOL of the head of the accepted queue. A second idle toggle, or a toggle with no pending segment, still raises spurious_sck. Payload and phase checks are not skipped. hand/wrong_cpol1_payload fails at a real sample, and boundary/negative/wrong_cpol_at_select fails CPOL at CSB assertion. Residual gap: an idle-level change driven by an offered but not-yet-accepted command (cmd_off) would be flagged. No control exercises this, so the possible false alarm is unvalidated.

The expected edge count is 2*n*8/width. TX visits enabled lanes in order 0..3, MSB-first per byte, and flushes the partial word at segment end. RX packs into lanes 7:0 upward with zero HIGH padding. All of this matches the registered amendment and the examples. It is justified by theory 412-419 and 483. Superseded lines 698-702 and 735-740 are retained as history. The Dual/Quad lane significance matches line 419. Negative controls cover: reversed lanes, nonzero padding, wrong low byte, wrong TX bit, zero_be_then_payload and sparse BE.

An event is confirmed only by an overdue selected SCK edge, never by flags. Both flag_only controls produce no event. Benign-delay controls behave correctly: tx_refill_260 to 268 and rx_one_cycle_hold produce no event, and tx_refill_300 produces one. The ev() window starts at segment acceptance (or at the reset trigger), so earlier payload faults make it dirty. Confirmed results: dirty_tx, dirty_rx and dirty_starvation are fail; clock_during_tx_stall is fail. Truncated runs give pending or no event, never pass. done() requires sdone, a CSB rise when CSAAT=0, every RX word observed, and resolved RX bits.

At the old cutoffs, the elapsed time equals exactly CLKDIV+1. An edge at that moment is still legal, so there is no witnessed pause. Requiring an event there would have to rely on flag evidence. The obligation is preserved, not weakened:
- The original traces now forbid success.
- New prefixes one cycle later require pending, and they are pending.
- The original failures are archived.

CSAAT release is permitted only by an accepted, or stably offered, next segment with a different CSID or configuration. Offers with valid=0 never permit release (self-test plus the premature_held_cs_release fault). partial_then_csid_switch and pending_cpol_csid_change pass. boundary/same_csid_config_change keeps a failure as a DUT-versus-theory 241-249 conflict. It is correctly not waived, and it is not claimed as a production bug. Its sck_phase failures are cascade noise, not separate defects.

Hardware reset clears the queue, words and rxexp, so stale TX data would surface as underflow or mismatch, and stale RX data as rx_unexpected_word. The supporting controls are one positive (hardware_abort_restart), one CSB fault and one truncation. There is no injected stale-payload-after-hardware-reset negative control, so stale-data detection is argued from code, not demonstrated. An abort is recorded only if the segment had already started edges; a reset that hits a queued but unstarted segment yields no event. Software reset is correctly labelled pass_unresolved, giving an inconclusive verdict.

An event is declared if any selected edge exceeds last+half while rx_valid&!rx_ready is held. An implementation-dependent transient inter-byte gap (theory 584) that coincides with a multi-cycle benign hold could be labelled backpressure. That would be a mislabelled event, not a false failure. Only a one-cycle hold is controlled.

There are 14 negatives and 13 credited detections. The uncredited one is negative/missing_rx_word, which by design gives inconclusive with no invented timeout. Unsupported speed or bidirectional segments are blocked. After a dummy segment, later segments never complete, so the outcome is inconclusive with no false pass.

The driver replays inputs only and contains no expected values. Timing is pre at +4, edge at +5, post at +9. The validator rejects illegal or out-of-width inputs and transfers during reset. The checker and controls are hash-pinned. No DUT internals are used. Eighteen omitted raw traces were not inspected; only their diagnostics were reviewed.

limitations: Read-only review of the supplied packet. Nothing was executed, and there is no proof of checker correctness or completeness.
Dummy-segment semantics and software-reset completion or data disposition remain unresolved obligations.
The same-CSID config-change-after-CSAAT conflict stays open pending upstream interpretation.
There is no negative control for stale data after hardware reset, for an unaccepted-offer CPOL idle change, or for a long benign RX hold coinciding with a transient gap.
The 18 omitted traces were not inspected.
Only two-state signals and the core boundary are covered: no TLUL, FIFOs or four-state behaviour.
This review grants no B/C authorization and makes no coverage, equivalence or formal claim.
